Filed `docs/ref/VAST_DEEP_GROK_ECONOMICS.md` — Vast as the external cost oracle for house **gstd** (proof-of-cost receipts), not gstdcoin.

**What the market actually is.** Hosts set GPU $/hr, storage, bandwidth, min-bid floor, and reserved-discount cap. Vast does not publish a rate card. Renter invoices have three meters: GPU (per second while active), storage (per second while the instance *exists*, stop does not stop it), bandwidth (per byte both ways).

**Numbers worth keeping (dated).** This house’s 2026-08-27 probe: 4090 **$0.121–$0.241/hr**, 3090 **$0.082–$0.162**, V100 from **$0.029**, RTX PRO 6000 Utah **$1.002** at reliability2 0.991. GPU Finder same day: cheapest in-stock 4090 **$0.13/hr**, H100 **$1.33/hr**. Storage samples cluster **~$0.20/GB/month** (this repo had been using ~$0.10). Bandwidth often **~$2.60/TB**, horror prints **$25/TB**. Host cut in the official FAQ is **75/25**, not the 85/15 third-party figure.

**Interruptible.** `min_bid` is a power-cost *floor*, not a price. Highest bid runs; any on-demand rental on those GPUs kills it. Vast publishes **no preemption frequency**. Bid API bounds: **$0.001–$32/hr**.

**Reserved.** Prepaid, locked to one machine. Marketing says up to 50%; the prepay API says typically **40%**; the worked example is **20%** for one month ($576 vs $720) with a **5%** early-exit clawback.

**Banned work.** Card-purchased credits: **crypto mining banned** (ToS 22). Uncensored LLM inference is **not named**; Vast ships Oobabooga/vLLM/Ollama guides. Still bound by the unlawful/hateful-content clause and export rules.

**gstd mint rule.** Receipts from **Charges rows** (GPU + disk + up + down), never from `min_bid` or GPU Finder’s false “egress free.”
